message: Select a card (1 more) to put on the bottom of your library
annotation_description: Bottomed a Swamp when the kept hand contains Cruel Ultimatum (UUBBBRR) and Army of the Damned (5BBB), both requiring heavy black mana. The only black source in the kept hand is Grixis Panorama. Temple of the False God is a much weaker card to keep as it does nothing until 5 lands are in play, and Illusionist's Gambit is highly situational.

Deflecting Palm is a reactive combat trick that prevents damage from a source and deals that damage back to its controller. Casting it during your own precombat main phase on turn 2 when no one is attacking or dealing damage means it accomplishes absolutely nothing - there is no source of damage to choose, so the spell is completely wasted. This throws away a potentially powerful card for zero value.

With a hand full of expensive cards (Mulldrifter 5, Sun Titan 6, Surtland Elementalist 7) and only 3 lands on board, Sonnet Timmy needs to find lands urgently. Foretelling Behold the Multiverse would set up a cheap Scry 2 + Draw 2 for next turn at just {1}{U}, helping find crucial land drops. Swiftfoot Boots does nothing with no creatures on board and the creatures it would protect are many turns away.

Missed a land drop on turn 3 with Transguild Promenade in hand. With a hand full of expensive spells (Wild Ricochet at 4 mana, Jaya's Immolating Inferno needing X+RR), getting to 4 lands next turn is important. They had 3 untapped lands to pay the {1} ETB cost, and nothing productive to do with the remaining 2 mana this turn.

GLM47 Heckler cast Timely Ward before playing their land (Transguild Promenade) for the turn. While both could be done this turn (play Transguild Promenade paying {1}, then cast Timely Ward for {2}{W} with remaining lands), casting the spell first means if something goes wrong or priorities change, the land drop is wasted. Standard practice is to play lands before casting spells to maximize information and flexibility.

Fetching 2 Plains when the hand is heavily blue-leaning (Behold the Multiverse, Mulldrifter, Surtland Elementalist needing UU, Windfall all need blue). With only Island and Azorius Guildgate as current blue sources, adding no Islands makes it very difficult to cast Surtland Elementalist (UU) and creates unnecessary color problems.

Should play a land before spending mana on leveling up Echo Mage. Playing Temple of the False God first would give 8 mana total (Temple produces 2 with 5+ lands), allowing both Mirari (5 mana) and a level up on Echo Mage (2 mana) in the same turn, rather than just a level up.
Fetched Mountain when already having 3 Mountains and only 1 Plains, with two white spells in hand (Dawn Charm, Condemn). Plains would better balance the mana base for the white-heavy hand.

message: Select a permanent card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard
annotation_description: Burnished Hart would have been significantly better here. Sun Titan is already on the battlefield without haste, so Swiftfoot Boots doesn't enable an immediate attack - Sun Titan can't attack this turn regardless since it was just cast in postcombat main. Burnished Hart comes back to the battlefield and can be sacrificed for 3 mana to fetch two basic lands, providing substantial ramp. With 7 lands, getting to 9 lands would help cast expensive cards like Surtland Elementalist (7 mana). Swiftfoot Boots only costs 1 to equip, but the hexproof/haste is less impactful than ramping by 2 lands when you have expensive cards in hand.

GLM47 Heckler targeted themselves with Jaya's Immolating Inferno, dealing 3 damage to their own face for no reason. The spell deals X damage to up to three targets, and they chose themselves as one of the three targets alongside two opponents. There is absolutely no benefit to dealing 3 damage to yourself.

With 5 white sources and only 3 blue sources, and a hand containing Surtland Elementalist (5UU), Mulldrifter (4U), Behold the Multiverse (3U), and Windfall (2U), fetching a Plains is wasteful. The mana base is already white-heavy and the hand is entirely blue-demanding. Plus there's a Plains in hand to play next turn.

Player misunderstood Rousing Refrain's effect entirely, thinking it deals damage rather than generating red mana equal to the target opponent's hand size. The optimal target should be whichever opponent has the most cards in hand to maximize mana generation. Sonnet Timmy, having deployed a 6-mana Sun Titan, likely has fewer cards in hand than other opponents.

message: Choose spell or ability to playWarhorn Blast
chosen_display: 1. Cast Warhorn Blast: Creatures you control get +2/+1 until end of turn.
annotation_description: Sonnet Timmy cast Warhorn Blast for its full cost of 4W (5 mana) to pump only a single creature (Sun Titan) by +2/+1, making it an 8/7 instead of 6/6 for one attack. This is very poor value - spending 5 mana and a card for +2 damage. Foretelling it for 2 mana now and casting it later for 2W would save 2 mana total, and more importantly, the card could be saved for a turn when there are multiple creatures to buff. With only Sun Titan on the board, the +2/+1 buff is minimal impact for a full card. Additionally, casting it at full cost leaves Sonnet Timmy with less mana available, when foretelling would preserve the card for a more impactful future turn while only costing 2 mana now.

Fetching 2 Plains when nearly every card in hand requires blue mana (Behold the Multiverse, Surtland Elementalist needing UU, Windfall). While there's an Island in hand to play, fetching at least 1 Island would provide more reliable access to the UU needed for Surtland Elementalist and general blue mana requirements.

Guttersnipe is a 2/2 creature that deals 2 damage to each opponent when you cast instants/sorceries, which synergizes well with Mirari already on the battlefield. However, Arcane Melee (reducing instant/sorcery costs by 2) also synergizes powerfully with Mirari and the spell-heavy deck. With 8 mana available (Island, Swamp, Izzet Guildgate, Island, Swamp, Swamp, Mirari, Mountain), casting Arcane Melee for 5 mana would leave 3 mana open (enough to potentially copy spells with Mirari next turn for cheaper). Guttersnipe costs 3 mana but is vulnerable as a 2/2 creature - it could be easily killed. Arcane Melee as an enchantment is harder to remove and provides immediate cost reduction that compounds with Mirari. That said, Guttersnipe provides damage output and the choice is defensible since the player also has Illusionist's Gambit for defense. The decision is close but Arcane Melee might have been slightly better given the Mirari synergy and greater resilience.

Casting Arcane Melee before playing Temple of the False God from hand. Playing the land first would provide additional mana (Temple adds {C}{C} with 5+ lands) and leave mana open after casting Arcane Melee, giving more flexibility to respond to threats or hold up Illusionist's Gambit.

Casting Flickerwisp during postcombat main means the exiled permanent returns at this turn's end step, making the exile nearly meaningless. If targeting Sun Titan, it actually gives the opponent a free ETB trigger to recur a permanent like Burnished Hart. Additionally, Flickerwisp would die to Heckler's own Winds of Rath in hand, making the creature investment potentially wasteful.

Flickerwisp's temporary exile was used on Swiftfoot Boots, which is relatively low-impact since the equipment just returns at end step and can be re-equipped. Mirari on Grok4F Libby's board is a much more threatening permanent that enables spell copying, and denying it for a turn cycle would be more impactful.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Cast Windfall for free instead of Behold the Multiverse, discarding Behold the Multiverse and an Island while giving all three opponents fresh hands. Behold the Multiverse for free would provide Scry 2 + draw 2 (pure card advantage) without helping opponents. Windfall symmetrically refills everyone's hands, which is especially dangerous when Grok4F Libby is at 40 life with 8 lands untapped and Sonnet Timmy only discarded 2 cards.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking Sonnet Timmy with Guttersnipe when Sun Titan (6/6 vigilance) can block and kill the 2/2 Guttersnipe. Guttersnipe is Libby's most valuable creature due to its triggered ability dealing 2 damage to each opponent on instant/sorcery casts. While Sonnet Timmy likely won't block over 2 damage, the risk of losing Guttersnipe is unnecessary.

GLM47 Heckler passed on using Word of Seizing to steal Sonnet Timmy's Sun Titan during combat. Stealing Sun Titan with split second, then attacking with it would trigger its attack ability to recur a permanent with MV ≤3 from the graveyard (e.g., Evolving Wilds, Terramorphic Expanse), while also dealing 6 damage and denying Sonnet Timmy a blocker for the turn.

GLM47 Heckler is enchanting Sram, Senior Edificer with Spirit Mantle, but Sram is their own creature that appears to be a 2/2 legendary. While Sram draws a card when an Aura is cast (which triggers here), putting Spirit Mantle on Sram gives it +1/+1 and protection from creatures, making it a 3/3 unblockable attacker. However, Flickerwisp (3/1 flyer) is already a better attacker, and Sun Titan (6/6 with vigilance) belonging to Sonnet Timmy is a much bigger threat on the board. The Spirit Mantle on Flickerwisp would make a 4/2 unblockable flyer, which deals more damage per turn. On the other hand, Sram with Spirit Mantle creates a Voltron engine where future Auras and Equipment draw cards and the creature can't be blocked by creatures. This is a reasonable strategic choice for building toward a Voltron plan, especially since Sram's draw trigger already fired. The choice between Flickerwisp and Sram is debatable - Flickerwisp might get flickered or die more easily as a 3/1, while Sram as a Voltron target has long-term value with its card draw ability.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Spectral Deluge with only 1 Island on the battlefield means X=1, so it only bounces creatures with toughness 1 or less. This wastes a powerful late-game sweeper for minimal impact (only bouncing Flickerwisp). With 2 Islands still in hand, waiting to play more Islands would have made this card significantly more powerful.

message: Select artifact or enchantment (selected 0 of 2, min 1)
annotation_description: Spirit Mantle is likely enchanting Sun Titan, making it a 7/7 with protection from creatures (unblockable, can't be blocked). This is a far more dangerous combination than Swiftfoot Boots, which only provides hexproof and haste to its equipped creature. An unblockable Sun Titan that recurs permanents every attack is one of the most threatening board states possible.

Spiteful Visions deals 1 damage to each player whenever they draw a card, and gives each player an extra draw per turn. In a multiplayer game where one opponent (Haiku Stoic) is already eliminated, Grok4F Libby is at 40 life (the highest), GLM47 Heckler is at 23, and Sonnet Timmy is at 35. While Spiteful Visions does asymmetrically hurt the lower-life players more, it also gives all opponents extra cards and hurts Libby too. Sonnet Timmy has Sun Titan on board and will benefit from extra draws to find more threats. Charmbreaker Devils (5R) would be castable with 8 lands and would start recurring instants/sorceries from the graveyard while being a 4/4 threat. Decree of Pain (6BB) is not yet castable. The Spiteful Visions play is defensible as it pressures the lower-life Heckler, but giving Sonnet Timmy (who has Sun Titan and a developed board) extra cards is risky.

Sonnet Timmy cast Cloudblazer before playing Island from hand and before attacking with Sun Titan. Playing Island first would give 8 lands, meaning after casting Cloudblazer (5 mana), they'd have 3 mana remaining - enough for Ghostly Prison. Additionally, attacking with Sun Titan first would trigger its attack ability to return a permanent with MV 3 or less from graveyard (e.g., Burnished Hart for ramp) before committing mana to Cloudblazer.

chosen_display: 2. Incendiary Command deals 2 damage to each creature.
annotation_description: Dealing 2 damage to each creature when the only creature on board is Sun Titan (6/6) accomplishes virtually nothing - it survives easily. This mode is wasted.

Cast Brass Squire, a 1/3 whose only ability is attaching equipment, with no equipment on the battlefield or in hand. Meanwhile, Flickerwisp was available as a 3/1 flyer that could temporarily exile Sun Titan (the biggest threat on board) and provide meaningful board presence.

Sonnet Timmy cast Day of the Dragons with only Sun Titan on the battlefield, exiling their powerful 6/6 vigilance creature to create just one 5/5 flying Dragon token. Sun Titan's recurring ETB/attack ability to return permanents from graveyard is extremely valuable (can recur Burnished Hart, Mulldrifter, etc.), and trading it for a single 5/5 flyer is a poor exchange. Additionally, Day of the Dragons as an enchantment is vulnerable to removal - if it's destroyed, the Dragon is sacrificed and Sun Titan returns, but the opponent could also just destroy it at an inopportune time. More importantly, Sonnet Timmy should have considered playing their land (Island or Plains) first before casting spells, and could have used Momentary Blink or Eerie Interlude on Sun Titan to get another ETB trigger to recur something from the graveyard first, THEN cast Day of the Dragons to exile and convert creatures (including any creatures returned by Sun Titan). Alternatively, Cleansing Nova could clear GLM47 Heckler's remaining board or destroy artifacts/enchantments.

Sonnet Timmy passed without activating Cryptic Caves to draw a card. With 5+ lands controlled and no immediate need for the colorless mana, sacrificing Cryptic Caves for a card draw would have been pure value. Additionally, they should have played a land (Island or Plains from hand) if they hadn't already this turn to maintain land development. The reasoning about 'DRAGONS ready' doesn't match the board state where they have no creatures.

Cast Mask of Avacyn before playing a land drop. They have several lands in hand (Slayers' Stronghold, Stone Quarry, Forgotten Cave, Rupture Spire) and should play a land first before casting spells. Slayers' Stronghold in particular provides excellent utility with its haste/vigilance activation. Additionally, casting Mask with no creatures on board is low-impact when Flickerwisp could be cast first to provide a body.

Declined to activate Evolving Wilds, which is a free activation that thins the deck and provides an additional land. There's no downside to cracking Evolving Wilds at any point since it's pure upside.

Declined to crack Evolving Wilds during upkeep. With Dimir Guildgate in hand as a land drop, sacrificing Evolving Wilds would net an additional land on battlefield (searching for a basic), ramping from 8 to potentially 10 lands this turn. This is pure upside mana development.

Sonnet Timmy has no creatures on the battlefield but believed they had four 5/5 dragons. They skipped their entire precombat main phase without playing a land (Island in hand) or casting any spells. They had mana available for Sea Gate Oracle (2U) to get a body and card selection, and could have played Island first for additional mana. Against the only remaining opponent at 34 life, developing the board is critical.

Sea Gate Oracle is on the stack, and Sonnet Timmy has Restoration Angel in hand which could flash in to flicker the Sea Gate Oracle when it enters the battlefield, drawing an extra card (getting two Sea Gate Oracle triggers instead of one). This is a clear value opportunity being missed. Additionally, Momentary Blink could serve the same purpose after the Oracle resolves. The player declined all options citing being 'stuck in a loop' rather than recognizing the value play.

Casting Soulherder with no creatures on the battlefield means it's just a 1/1 body with no immediate blink value. Restoration Angel is a much better standalone creature as a 3/4 flyer that applies real pressure in a 1v1 against an opponent at 34 life.

message: Select another target creature you control
annotation_description: Failed to activate Cryptic Caves to draw a card at end of turn with unused mana. Sonnet Timmy controls 8 lands (meeting the 5+ requirement) and has untapped Plains to pay the {1} cost. With an Island in hand ready to play next turn, sacrificing the colorless-only Cryptic Caves for a card draw is good value.

Declined to crack Evolving Wilds when there was no reason not to. Cracking it during the beginning phase means the fetched land enters tapped now and will be available untapped on the next turn. It's pure upside - deck thinning and mana fixing at no cost.

Declined to activate Evolving Wilds, which is a free mana-fixing/deck-thinning activation with no downside. In a 1v1 situation against Sonnet Timmy, getting an untapped basic land and thinning the deck is pure upside.

Declined to crack Evolving Wilds for a free land fetch, missing deck thinning and mana fixing. With expensive cards in hand like Wild Ricochet (2RR) and Terra Ravager (2RR), getting an extra land onto the battlefield is valuable.

Discarded Terra Ravager, one of the best remaining threats that could swing for 8+ damage, while keeping Tempt with Reflections which requires a creature on the battlefield (Libby has none). Terra Ravager would have served as both a body and a significant damage source.

Declined to activate Evolving Wilds during upkeep, missing an opportunity to get an additional basic land onto the battlefield. Since the player has a land in hand (Dimir Guildgate or Island) to play as their normal land drop, sacrificing Evolving Wilds would effectively ramp them from 8 to 9 lands, which helps cast multiple spells or higher-cost spells in upcoming turns.

message: Select artifact or enchantment (selected 0 of 2, min 1)
annotation_description: With both Propaganda and Ghostly Prison on the battlefield taxing attacks against Grok4F Libby (the sole remaining opponent), exiling only one tax effect still leaves a {2}-per-creature attack tax. At 8 lands, paying {2} per attacker significantly limits combat pressure. Spiteful Visions, while annoying, is manageable at 21 life and could even be used strategically.

message: Choose spell or ability to playDecree of Pain
chosen_display: 1. Cast Decree of Pain: Destroy all creatures. They can't be regenerated. Draw a card for each creature destroyed this way.
annotation_description: Cast Decree of Pain for full cost (8 mana) with zero creatures on the battlefield, resulting in destroying nothing and drawing zero cards. The spell accomplished absolutely nothing while consuming the entire turn's mana.

message: Select card to discard (selected 1 of 6, min 6)
annotation_description: Discarding Sudden Spoiling (a split-second combat trick that's excellent defense at 11 life) while apparently keeping Tempt with Reflections, which requires a creature you control to target and Libby has zero creatures on the battlefield, making it currently uncastable.
